summary: A **scalar** has magnitude only (mass, speed, distance, energy, time, temperature). A **vector** has both magnitude and direction (force, velocity, acceleration, weight, displacement, momentum).
formulas: Period T = total time / N oscillations
points: **Measuring Cylinder & Parallax Error:** Read the **bottom of the meniscus** with your eye **perpendicular** to the scale.
**Simple Pendulum:** Time **20 oscillations** from the centre fiducial mark and divide by 20 to reduce human reaction-time error.
**Micrometer Screw Gauge:** Precision `0.01 mm` (main scale + thimble reading minus any zero error).
examiner_trap: Speed and distance are scalars; velocity, displacement, force, weight, and momentum are vectors.

summary: Motion graphs describe speed, acceleration, and distance travelled using **gradient (slope)** and **area under the graph**.
points: **Distance–Time Graph:** Gradient = **speed**. Horizontal line = at rest (`speed = 0`); straight line sloping up = constant speed; curve getting steeper = acceleration; curve getting flatter = deceleration.

**Speed–Time Graph:** Gradient = **acceleration**; **Area under graph** = **distance travelled**. Horizontal line = constant speed (`a = 0`); straight upward line = uniform acceleration; downward line = uniform deceleration.
examiner_trap: A horizontal line on a **speed–time** graph means **constant speed** (not at rest, unless `speed = 0`).

topic: Free Fall, Vertical Throw & Terminal Velocity
summary: Gravity accelerates all objects near Earth downwards at `g ≈ 9.8 m/s²` regardless of mass (when air resistance is negligible).
points: **Ball Thrown Vertically Upwards (at the highest point):** Instantaneous **velocity is `0 m/s`**, but **acceleration is STILL `9.8 m/s²` downwards** because Earth's gravitational force (weight) still acts downwards.

**Terminal Velocity:** Initially `weight > air resistance` so object accelerates downwards. As speed rises, air resistance increases, reducing resultant force and acceleration until **air resistance = weight** (`resultant force = 0`, constant terminal velocity).

**Opening a Parachute:** Surface area increases sharply → air resistance suddenly becomes **greater than weight** → net upward force → object decelerates until a new, lower terminal velocity is reached.

**Why Astronauts Feel Weightless in Orbit:** Gravity STILL acts on them (providing centripetal force), but both the astronaut and spacecraft are in **continuous free fall** together around Earth, so there is zero normal contact force.
examiner_trap: Never write 'gravity becomes zero' at the top of a throw or in Earth orbit — gravity still acts!

summary: **Mass** (`kg`) is the amount of matter (stays constant everywhere). **Weight** (`N`) is the gravitational force on a mass (`W = m × g`). **Density** (`ρ = m / V`) determines whether an object floats or sinks.
formulas: W = m × g  (g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth)
points: **Why a steel ship floats:** The ship is hollow and contains **air spaces**, so its **overall average density** is **less than the density of water**.
**Irregular Solid Density:** Measure mass on a digital balance; measure volume by water displacement in a measuring cylinder or **displacement (Eureka) can**; compute `ρ = m / V`.
**Earth vs Moon:** **Mass stays constant**, whereas **weight decreases** on the Moon because `g` is smaller (`≈ 1.6 N/kg`).
examiner_trap: Mass is measured in `kg` on a balance; weight is a force measured in `N` with a newton-meter.

topic: Forces, Newton's Laws, Hooke's Law & Circular Motion
summary: A **resultant force** changes an object's speed, direction (circular motion), or shape (Hooke's law).
points: **Newton's 1st Law (Inertia):** An object stays at rest or continues at **constant velocity** unless acted upon by a non-zero **resultant force**.
**Newton's 2nd Law:** `F = m × a` — resultant force equals mass × acceleration (in the same direction).
**Newton's 3rd Law:** Body A exerts a force on B; B exerts an **equal in magnitude, opposite in direction** force of the **same type** on A.
**Hooke's Law:** Extension (`x`) is directly proportional to load (`F`) up to the **limit of proportionality**.
**Circular Motion:** Even at constant speed, **velocity changes** because **direction changes continuously**, requiring a **resultant centripetal force towards the centre**.
examiner_trap: On an extension–load graph, the **limit of proportionality** is the point where the straight line starts to curve.

summary: The **moment of a force** measures its turning effect about a pivot: `Moment = Force × perpendicular distance from pivot`.
formulas: Equilibrium: Σ Clockwise moments = Σ Anticlockwise moments
points: **Two Conditions for Equilibrium:** (1) **No resultant force** (`ΣF = 0`), and (2) **No resultant moment** (`ΣM = 0`) about any pivot.
**Stability:** Lower **centre of gravity** and wider **base** give greater stability. An object topples when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base.
**Irregular Lamina Centre of Gravity:** Hang freely from a pin and draw vertical lines using a **plumb line** from two different holes; their intersection is the centre of gravity.
examiner_trap: Always state **perpendicular distance** from the pivot — omitting 'perpendicular' loses the definition mark.

summary: **Pressure** is force per unit perpendicular area (`p = F / A`). Liquid pressure increases with depth and density (`Δp = ρ g Δh`).
points: **Small Area vs Large Area:** A sharp knife concentrates force onto a tiny area (`high pressure`); snowshoes spread weight over a large area (`low pressure`).
**Liquid Pressure:** Acts equally in all directions at the same depth and does not depend on container shape.
**Mercury Barometer:** Atmospheric pressure supports a `~760 mm` column of mercury (`p = ρ g h`); vacuum sits above the mercury.
examiner_trap: Convert `cm²` to `m²` by dividing by `10,000` (`1 m² = 10⁴ cm²`) before computing Pascals (`Pa`).

summary: Energy is conserved and transferred between stores (**kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic, thermal, chemical, nuclear**).
points: **Speed vs Kinetic Energy:** Because `E_k = ½ m v²`, doubling speed increases kinetic energy by **4×** (`2²`).
**Power:** Work done / energy transferred per second (`1 W = 1 J/s`).
**Wasted Energy:** Usually transferred to the surroundings as **thermal (internal) energy** due to friction or air resistance.
examiner_trap: Distance `d` in `W = F × d` must be moved **in the direction of the force**.

summary: **Momentum** (`p = m × v`) is conserved in closed systems where no external resultant force acts.
formulas: p = m × v  (kg m/s or N s)
Impulse = F × Δt = Δp = mv − mu
points: **Airbags & Crumple Zones:** Increase the **collision time (`Δt`)** for the same change in momentum (`Δp`), so the **rate of change of momentum (`F = Δp/Δt`) decreases**, reducing the force on the passenger.
**Vector Sign:** Assign `+` to one direction and `−` to the opposite direction during collisions or explosions.
examiner_trap: Never say airbags 'reduce momentum' — the momentum change is unchanged; airbags **increase impact time** so **force decreases**.

topic: Kinetic Particle Theory, Brownian Motion & Gas Laws
summary: Particles in matter are in continuous random motion; average kinetic energy of molecules increases with **Kelvin temperature**.
points: **Brownian Motion:** Visible smoke/pollen particles move randomly in zig-zag paths because **invisible, fast-moving air/water molecules collide randomly** with them from all directions.

**Gas Pressure:** Gas molecules collide with container walls, changing momentum and exerting a **force per unit area**. Heating a gas makes molecules move **faster** → **more frequent and harder collisions** with the walls → pressure increases.
**Compressing Gas at Constant Temperature (`p₁V₁ = p₂V₂`):** Smaller volume means molecules travel shorter distances between collisions → **more frequent collisions** with walls → higher pressure.
examiner_trap: Always mention BOTH **more frequent** collisions AND **greater force / harder** collisions when temperature rises!

summary: **Evaporation** happens at any temperature below boiling point when the **most energetic molecules escape from the liquid surface**.
formulas: Faster evaporation: higher temperature, larger surface area, air draught/wind, lower humidity
points: **Why Evaporation Causes Cooling:** Only the **fastest (highest kinetic energy) molecules** overcome intermolecular forces and escape from the surface, so the **average kinetic energy** of the remaining molecules decreases → **temperature drops**.

**Evaporation vs Boiling:** Evaporation happens at **any temperature** and **at the surface only** (no bubbles). Boiling happens at a **fixed boiling point** throughout the **entire liquid** (bubbles form).
examiner_trap: State that **average** kinetic energy of the remaining molecules decreases (not that all molecules stop moving).

summary: When heated, particles vibrate/move faster and push further apart, causing **expansion** (gases > liquids > solids).
points: **Bimetallic Strip:** Two different metals bonded together expand by different amounts when heated, causing the strip to **bend** (used in thermostats & fire alarms).
**Railway & Bridge Gaps:** Prevent buckling on hot days when solids expand.
**Liquid-in-Glass Thermometer:** Narrower bore increases **sensitivity**; larger bulb increases **sensitivity** (reduces range unless stem is longer).
examiner_trap: Remember **gases expand far more than liquids, which expand more than solids** for the same temperature rise.

summary: Thermal energy transfers by **conduction** (mainly solids), **convection** (fluids: liquids & gases), and **infrared radiation** (EM waves — works in a vacuum).
formulas: Convection requires fluid density change; Radiation requires no medium
points: **Conduction (Metals vs Non-Metals):** Atoms vibrate faster and pass kinetic energy to neighbours. Metals conduct far faster because they have **delocalised (free) electrons** that move rapidly through the lattice and collide with ions.

**Why a Metal Spoon Feels Colder Than Wood at Room Temperature:** Both are at the same temperature, but metal is a **good thermal conductor**, so it conducts heat **away from your hand much faster** than wood (an insulator).
**Convection (Fluids Only):** Heated fluid **expands** → its **density decreases** → warmer, less dense fluid **rises** while cooler, denser fluid **sinks**, creating a **convection current**.
**Infrared Radiation:** **Dull, black surfaces** are the **best emitters and absorbers**; **shiny, silver/white surfaces** are **poor emitters/absorbers and good reflectors**.
**Heat Lost vs Heat Gained (Notes p.80):** Heat supplied `<` heat lost → temperature falls; equal → constant; greater → rises.
examiner_trap: Convection **never** occurs in solids (particles fixed) or in a vacuum (no particles); **radiation** is the only transfer method through a vacuum.

summary: **Specific Heat Capacity (`c`)** is the thermal energy needed to raise `1 kg` by `1 °C`. During melting or boiling, temperature stays constant because energy breaks intermolecular bonds.
formulas: E = P × t = V × I × t
points: **Why Temperature Stays Constant During Melting/Boiling:** Supplied thermal energy increases **internal potential energy** to overcome/break **intermolecular forces/bonds**, instead of increasing the average kinetic energy of molecules.
**Experiment Precaution:** Insulate the block/beaker with lagging and stir liquids gently to reduce heat lost to surroundings (measured `c` would otherwise be **too high**).
examiner_trap: Convert mass from **grams to kilograms (`÷ 1000`)** when `c` is in `J/(kg °C)`.

summary: Insulators become charged by friction when **electrons** are transferred (protons never move). An **electric field** is a region where an electric charge experiences a force.
formulas: Like charges repel; unlike charges attract
Field arrow direction = force on a positive charge (+ → −)
points: **Charging by Friction:** Polythene rubbed with cloth gains **electrons** (becomes negative); perspex/acetate loses **electrons** (becomes positive).
**Electric Field Patterns:** Radial outward from `+`, radial inward to `−`; uniform parallel lines between opposite parallel plates.
**Earthing Fuel Pipes:** Fuel flowing causes friction & charge build-up; earthing wires discharge static safely to prevent sparks.
examiner_trap: Always say **electrons** move — **never** say positive protons move when explaining static charging.

topic: Charge, Current, Voltage, Resistance & I–V Graphs
summary: **Current (`I = Q/t`)** is rate of flow of charge. **Potential difference (`V = E/Q`)** is work done per unit charge. **Ohm's Law** states `I ∝ V` at constant temperature.
points: **Ohmic Resistor `I–V` Graph:** Straight line through origin `(0, 0)` → constant resistance.

**Filament Lamp `I–V` Graph:** As current increases, the filament heats up → metal lattice ions vibrate more vigorously → **more frequent collisions with free electrons** → **resistance increases** and the graph flattens.
**Semiconductor Diode:** Conducts in **one direction only** (forward bias); very high resistance in reverse bias.
**Wire Length & Diameter:** Doubling length `L` doubles resistance; doubling diameter `d` increases area `4×` (`A = πr²`), reducing resistance to **`¼`**.
examiner_trap: Connect an **ammeter in series** (very low resistance) and a **voltmeter in parallel** (very high resistance).

topic: Electrical Power, kWh, Home Installation, Fuses & Safety
summary: Mains electricity (`230 V a.c., 50 Hz`) uses **live, neutral, and earth** wires. Fuses and circuit breakers prevent overheating and electric shock.
formulas: P = I V = I² R = V² / R
E = P t = V I t
points: **Fuse & Switch Position:** Always placed on the **live wire** so when the fuse melts or switch opens, the appliance is disconnected from high voltage.
**Earth Wire:** Connects metal casing to ground; if a loose live wire touches the casing, a huge current flows to earth and immediately **blows the fuse**.
**Double Insulation:** Plastic casing is an insulator — no earth wire needed.
examiner_trap: Choose a fuse rating **just above** the normal operating current (e.g. `4.2 A` normal → use **`5 A` fuse**, not `3 A` or `13 A`).

topic: Series/Parallel Circuits, Potential Dividers, LDRs, Thermistors & Relays
summary: In **series**, current is identical everywhere and voltages add (`V = V₁ + V₂`). In **parallel**, voltage across each branch equals the supply voltage and currents add (`I = I₁ + I₂`).
formulas: Potential divider: V₁ / V₂ = R₁ / R₂
points: **Adding a Bulb in Parallel:** Each parallel branch still receives the **full supply voltage**, so existing bulbs keep the **same brightness** (and if one breaks, others stay on), while total battery current increases.
**LDR & NTC Thermistor:** Increasing **light intensity** decreases an **LDR's** resistance; increasing **temperature** decreases a **thermistor's** resistance.
**Potential Divider Rule:** The component with the **larger resistance takes the larger share of the supply p.d.**
examiner_trap: When LDR resistance drops in bright light, the p.d. across the **LDR decreases** and the p.d. across the **fixed resistor increases**!

summary: Magnetic field lines run from **North to South** outside a magnet; closer lines indicate a **stronger magnetic field**.
formulas: Solenoid strength ↑ with: more turns, larger current, soft-iron core
points: **Soft Iron vs Steel:** **Soft iron** magnetises and demagnetises easily (temporary magnets: electromagnets & transformer cores); **steel** retains magnetism (permanent magnets).
**Right-Hand Grip Rule:** Thumb points along conventional current in a straight wire (or N-pole of solenoid); curled fingers show magnetic field direction.
**Demagnetisation:** Slowly withdraw magnet from an **a.c. solenoid**, or heat strongly / hammer while aligned E–W.
examiner_trap: Never say 'copper is magnetic' — only **iron, steel, nickel, and cobalt** are magnetic materials.

topic: Force on Current-Carrying Conductor & D.C. Motor
summary: A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field experiences a **force** perpendicular to both current and field (**Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**).
formulas: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: ThuMb = Motion/Force, First finger = Field (N→S), seCond finger = Current (+→−)
points: **D.C. Motor & Split-Ring Commutator:** The split-ring commutator **reverses the current direction in the coil every half-turn** (when vertical) so the turning force stays in the **same rotational direction** continuously.
**Increase Motor Turning Effect:** Increase current, use stronger magnets, add more coil turns, or insert a soft-iron core.
**Beam of Electrons/Protons:** Remember conventional current is **opposite** to electron flow direction when applying Fleming's Left-Hand Rule!
examiner_trap: Use **Left-Hand Rule** for **Motors** (force from current), and **Right-Hand Rule** for **Generators** (induced current from motion).

topic: Electromagnetic Induction, Lenz's Law & A.C. Generator
summary: An e.m.f. is induced whenever a conductor **cuts magnetic field lines** (or magnetic flux changes). **Lenz's Law** states the induced current opposes the change causing it.
formulas: Larger induced e.m.f.: faster motion, stronger magnet, more turns
points: **A.C. Generator (1st & 2nd Half Cycles — Notes p.148–150):** Uses **slip rings** and carbon brushes. Vertical coil → sides move parallel to field → **zero cutting, zero current**. Horizontal coil → cuts field lines at max rate → **maximum current** (reverses polarity every half-turn).
**Lenz's Law:** Pushing a North pole into a coil induces a **North pole** at that end to **oppose** the magnet's motion (conservation of energy).
examiner_trap: A.C. generators have **slip rings** (continuous contact); D.C. motors have a **split-ring commutator**.

summary: Transformers step alternating voltage up or down using mutual induction across a **laminated soft-iron core**.
formulas: Power loss in cables: P_loss = I² × R
points: **Why Transformers Need a.c. (and Fail With d.c.):** Alternating current creates a **continuously changing magnetic field** in the **soft-iron core** that cuts the secondary coil and induces e.m.f. Direct current creates a **constant magnetic field** (`no cutting` → zero induced voltage).

**High-Voltage Power Transmission:** Step-up transformers raise voltage to **reduce current** (`I = P/V`), drastically cutting thermal power loss **`I²R`** in transmission cables, allowing thinner/cheaper cables.
examiner_trap: Step-up transformers reduce **current** (not resistance) in cables, cutting `I²R` heating loss.

topic: Atomic Structure, Isotopes & Rutherford Gold-Foil Scattering
summary: An atom consists of a tiny, dense, positively charged **nucleus** (protons + neutrons) surrounded by orbiting electrons.
points: **Rutherford Gold Foil Experiment:** (1) Most α-particles pass straight through → **atom is mostly empty space**; (2) A few deflect slightly → **nucleus is positively charged**; (3) Very few bounce straight back → **nucleus is tiny and contains almost all the mass**.
examiner_trap: Isotopes have identical **chemical** properties (same electron arrangement) and different **physical** properties (different mass).

topic: Alpha, Beta, Gamma Radiation, Nuclear Fission & Fusion
summary: Unstable nuclei emit **alpha (`⁴₂He`)**, **beta (`⁰₋₁e`)**, or **gamma (`γ`)** radiation randomly and spontaneously.
points: **Penetration & Ionisation:** α is **most ionising** (stopped by paper / few cm air); β is moderate (stopped by `~3 mm` aluminium); γ is **most penetrating** (reduced by thick lead/concrete) and least ionising.
**Field Deflection:** α (`+2`) and β (`−1`) deflect in **opposite** directions in electric/magnetic fields (β deflects much more due to tiny mass); γ is uncharged and **undeflected**.

**Fission vs Fusion:** **Fission** splits a heavy nucleus (`U-235`) using a slow neutron; **Fusion** joins two light nuclei (hydrogen → helium) at extreme temperature & pressure (powers the Sun & stars).
examiner_trap: Gamma is **not** stopped completely by lead — its intensity is **reduced**.

summary: **Half-life (`t_½`)** is the average time taken for half the unstable nuclei in a sample to decay (or for corrected activity to halve).
formulas: Corrected count = Measured count − Background count
points: **Background Radiation Sources:** Radon gas (rocks), cosmic rays, medical X-rays, food & drink, nuclear fallout.

**Applications:** **Smoke detectors** use α (`Am-241`, short range & high ionisation); **paper/foil thickness** uses β; **medical tracers & sterilisation** use γ (penetrates out of body, short half-life).
**Safety:** Store in lead-lined boxes, handle with tongs, keep distance, wear film badges, minimise exposure time.
examiner_trap: ALWAYS subtract **background count rate** BEFORE calculating half-life, and add it back if asked for a GM detector reading!

topic: General Wave Properties, Diffraction & Ripple Tank
summary: Waves transfer **energy without transferring matter**. Wave speed `v = f × λ`.
points: **Transverse vs Longitudinal:** Transverse vibrates **perpendicular** to wave direction (light, water, all EM waves); Longitudinal vibrates **parallel** via compressions & rarefactions (sound).
**Diffraction:** Waves spread out through a gap/around an edge. **Greatest diffraction** when **gap width ≈ wavelength (`λ`)**. Wavelength, frequency, and speed stay **unchanged**.
**Deep → Shallow Water (Ripple Tank):** Speed **decreases**, wavelength **decreases**, **frequency stays constant**, wavefronts bend **towards normal**.
examiner_trap: During refraction or change of water depth, **frequency NEVER changes** (only speed and wavelength change).

summary: Sound is a **longitudinal mechanical wave** requiring a medium (`~330–340 m/s` in air, `~1500 m/s` in water, `~5000 m/s` in steel).
points: **Pitch & Loudness:** Higher **frequency** → higher **pitch**; larger **amplitude** → **louder** sound.
**Ultrasound (`f > 20,000 Hz`):** Used for **prenatal scanning**, detecting **cracks in metal**, and **sonar depth sounding** (`d = v × t / 2`).
examiner_trap: For echo or sonar problems, remember the sound travels **there AND back (`2d`)**!

summary: For reflection at any surface, **angle of incidence `i` = angle of reflection `r`** (both measured from the normal).
formulas: Image distance = Object distance behind mirror
points: **Plane Mirror Image Properties:** **Virtual** (cannot be formed on a screen), **upright**, **same size** as object, **laterally inverted**, and at the **same distance behind the mirror** as the object is in front.
examiner_trap: Always draw a dashed **virtual ray** behind the mirror and arrow directions on real rays.

topic: Refraction, Refractive Index, Critical Angle & Optical Fibres
summary: Light bends when changing speed across a boundary (`n = sin i / sin r`) and undergoes **Total Internal Reflection (TIR)** when `i > c` from dense to less dense medium.
formulas: n = sin i / sin r = c_air / v_medium
points: **Conditions for TIR:** (1) Light travels from **optically denser to less dense medium** (e.g. glass → air), AND (2) **angle of incidence > critical angle (`i > c`)**.
**Optical Fibres:** Light reflects repeatedly inside a high-index glass core by **TIR** — used in high-speed telecommunications (digital signals, less attenuation) and medical **endoscopes**.
examiner_trap: Measure angles `i` and `r` from the **normal**, never from the glass surface.

summary: All **electromagnetic waves** are **transverse**, travel at **`3.0 × 10⁸ m/s` in a vacuum**, and obey `c = f × λ`.
formulas: Order (increasing f / decreasing λ): Radio → Microwave → IR → Visible → UV → X-ray → Gamma
points: **Dispersion in a Prism:** White light splits into a spectrum because **violet** travels slowest in glass and refracts **most**, while **red** travels fastest and refracts **least**.

**EM Uses & Hazards:** Radio (broadcasting), Microwaves (satellite comms, cooking — internal tissue heating), IR (remotes, thermal cameras — skin burns), UV (fluorescent lamps, sterilisation — skin cancer/eye damage), X-rays (medical bones/security), Gamma (cancer radiotherapy, sterilising instruments).
examiner_trap: **Monochromatic** light has a **single frequency** (and single wavelength/colour).

topic: Converging & Diverging Lenses and Eye Defects
summary: A **converging (convex) lens** brings parallel rays to the **principal focus (`F`)**; a **diverging (concave) lens** spreads parallel rays outwards.
formulas: Focal length f = distance from optical centre to principal focus F
points: **Converging Lens Image Cases:** `u > 2f` → real, inverted, diminished (camera); `u = 2f` → real, inverted, same size; `f < u < 2f` → real, inverted, magnified (projector); **`u < f`** → **virtual, upright, magnified** (magnifying glass).
**Eye Defects:** **Short-sightedness** (focuses in front of retina) corrected by a **diverging lens**; **Long-sightedness** (focuses behind retina) corrected by a **converging lens**.
examiner_trap: A **real image** can be projected onto a screen; a **virtual image** cannot.

topic: Earth, Moon, Day/Night, Seasons & Lunar Phases
summary: Earth spins on its tilted axis (`23.5°`) every **24 hours** (day/night), orbits the Sun in **365 days** (seasons), and the Moon orbits Earth every **~27.3 days**.
formulas: Day = 24 hours; Year ≈ 365.25 days; Lunar month ≈ 27.3 days
points: **Seasons:** Caused by the **tilt of Earth's axis** (NOT distance to the Sun) — the hemisphere tilted towards the Sun receives more direct sunlight and longer days (summer).
**Phases of the Moon:** Caused by seeing different fractions of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth.
examiner_trap: Seasons are caused by Earth's **axial tilt**, NEVER by Earth getting closer to the Sun!

summary: Gravity provides the centripetal force keeping planets, moons, and comets in orbit around the Sun/planets.
formulas: Gravitational field strength decreases with distance from the Sun
points: **Order of Planets:** Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (small rocky inner planets) | Asteroid Belt | Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune (large gaseous/icy outer planets).
**Accretion Model:** Spinning cloud of dust & gas collapsed under gravity; inner hot region formed rocky planets, cooler outer region formed gas giants.
**Comet Orbits:** Elliptical orbit; comet moves **fastest when closest to the Sun** (GPE transfers to KE as gravitational attraction is strongest).
examiner_trap: Inner rocky planets formed because heavy elements with high melting points condensed close to the hot Sun.

summary: Stars form in **nebulae** and spend most of their lives on the **main sequence** fusing hydrogen into helium until nuclear fuel runs low.
points: **Main Sequence Stability:** **Inward gravitational pull balances outward thermal/radiation pressure** from core nuclear fusion.
**Sun-like (Low-Mass) Star:** Nebula → Protostar → Main Sequence → **Red Giant** → Planetary Nebula + **White Dwarf**.
**Massive Star:** Nebula → Protostar → Main Sequence → **Red Supergiant** → **Supernova** (spreads heavy elements) → **Neutron Star** or **Black Hole**.
examiner_trap: Elements heavier than iron are formed and scattered into space during a **supernova** explosion.

topic: The Universe, Redshift, Hubble's Law & The Big Bang
summary: **Galactic redshift** and **Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMBR)** provide key evidence that the Universe began ~13.8 billion years ago in a hot, dense **Big Bang** and is still expanding.
formulas: Age of Universe ≈ 1 / H₀ = d / v ≈ 4.5 × 10¹⁷ s
points: **Redshift:** Light from distant galaxies shows an **increase in observed wavelength** (shifted toward the red end), proving galaxies are moving away — **further galaxies recede faster** (`v = H₀ d`).
**CMBR:** Microwave radiation observed uniformly in **all directions** across space — redshifted leftover thermal radiation from the hot early Universe.
examiner_trap: Say redshift is an **increase in observed wavelength** (not 'the galaxy turns red').
